question: ________ deciphered Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts that were used for earlier inscriptions.
solution:
The correct answer is __**James Princep.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Prinsep**__ was an English scholar and the founding editor of the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal.
 
• James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts that were used for earlier inscriptions.
 
• In 1838, James Prinsep deciphered the letters Brahmi and Kharoshti, which were used in the oldest inscriptions and coinage.
 
• After Prinsep recognised the Kharosthi inscription's language as Prakrit, it became possible to interpret longer inscriptions.
 
• Apart from working as an assay master at the Benares Mint, he studied, documented, and illustrated various topics of numismatics, metallurgy, and meteorology.
 
• Christian Lassen, a Norwegian scholar, made the first successful attempts to interpret Brahmi in 1836.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Brahmi** is an ancient South Asian writing system.

 
 
• Most Prakrit inscriptions were written in the Brahmi script.
 
• Brahmi script used in most Ashokan inscriptions is the basis for the majority of scripts used to write current Indian languages.
 
 
 
• The **Kharosthi script **was an ancient Indian script used in areas of the Indian subcontinent and present-day eastern Afghanistan by the Khasa, Saka, and Yuezhi peoples.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sir Alexander Cunningham** was an archaeologist who excavated many sites in India, including Saranath and Sāanchi.

 
 
• He served as the first director of the Indian Archaeological Survey.
 
 
 
• **John Archibald Wheeler **was an American theoretical physicist who was instrumental in rekindling interest in general relativity in the United States following World War II.
